_readme: Single source of truth for every course date.
Dates are stored as (week, day) offsets, not calendar dates, so rolling the
course to a new year means editing the `term` block only -- every deadline,
midterm and release date moves with it.
week: 1 = the week containing term.first_class_day. Weeks start on Monday.
day : Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri.
anchor: 'term' (default) counts weeks from the first class week.
'finals' counts weeks from term.finals_week_starts, so week 1 of the
finals anchor is finals week itself.

_materials_readme: The Dropbox shared-folder link students use to download everything: the qmd
and its datasets, for every assignment.
Share assignments/students/<year>/ -- THE YEAR FOLDER, not students/ itself.
Sharing students/ would let a student wander into another year's folder and
download the wrong assignment. The year folder contains only that year.
It lives inside Dropbox, so `Rscript assignments/build-assignments.R`
publishes to students with no upload step.
ROLLING THE YEAR: after changing `term`, share the new year folder and
update BOTH `url` and `year` below. The build fails while `year` disagrees
with the term, so this cannot be silently forgotten.
NEVER share assignments/ or the repo root: that would expose keys/ (the
answer keys) and submission/ (other students' work).
